steps: Confirm the fireplace & codes

Approved masonry wood fireplace built to NFPA 211 (CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada), not a factory-built one. Never connect to a flue serving another appliance or to an air distribution duct; in a mobile home, not in a sleeping room.

Install to local and national codes and contact local building or fire officials about restrictions and inspection. Never install in a makeshift or "temporary" manner.

  • Connect to a code-approved masonry chimney with a listed flue liner.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance, or to any air distribution duct.
  • Mobile homes: do not install in a sleeping room.
  • Outside combustion air may be required locally.
Note: this page and the label (p. 25) rule out factory-built fireplaces; p. 11 refers to clearances "when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace."
Pacific Energy recommends installers certified by NFI or CSIA (USA), or WETT or APC (Canada).
Uncrate
Remove the wood top and supports, then the plastic cover. Remove the retaining clip on the front of the baffle before the first fire.
Inspect & prep the fireplace

Opening at least 29" wide at the front, 22" at the back, 20 1/4" high and 18" deep. Repair cracks or loose mortar, lock the damper open or remove it, and have the chimney cleaned; fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified.
Full flue liner
Required in Canada and highly recommended: a listed 6" stainless rigid or flex liner from the flue collar to the top of the chimney.

1. Measure the chimney height from the top of the existing flue to the floor of the hearth (leaves extra liner for flashing and rain cap).
  2. Feed the liner from the top of the chimney, through the damper area, into the fireplace cavity.
  3. Attach a stove connector to the bottom of the liner per the liner instructions.
  4. Push the insert into position, attach the connector to the stove collar and secure with screws. Level with the rear adjusting legs.
  5. Trim and shape a top flashing to the existing flue with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side; seat it on the tile, screw the flashing collar to the liner and caulk the gap with RTV silicone.
  6. Attach a rain cap to the end of the liner; a storm collar is optional.

Canada: continuous 6 inch liner meeting class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640.
Or: direct flue connection (USA only)
Listed stainless liner from the flue collar into the first masonry chimney flue liner, with a seal in the throat. Local codes may require a clean-out door.

1. Measure from the first chimney flue liner to the top of the insert, allowing extra length to insert into the flue tile.
  2. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile; seal around the pipe to the chimney with non-combustible materials.
  3. Attach a stove connector to the bottom of the liner.
  4. Push the insert into position, attach the connector to the stove collar and secure with screws.
Combustion air

Outside air: remove the ash clean-out cover, fit a rodent screen in its place and don't cover the air inlet opening. Room air: remove the cover plate beneath the ash lip (two screws) and make sure the room supplies adequate combustion air.
Level the insert
Screw the leveling leg bolts into the nuts in the base bottom to stabilize the unit on uneven surfaces.
Assemble & fit the surround

Remove the side-panel shipping screws and the fan controls, bolt top parts A, B and C together, hook the panels onto the bracket pins, then push the unit back until the surround meets the fireplace facing.

1. Remove the shipping screws at the top of each surround side panel and the two screws holding the fan controls; remove the controls and lift off both panels.
  2. Lay top-panel parts A, B and C face down on a flat, non-marking surface and fasten them with the 1/4" x 1/2" bolts and nuts at points "D".
  3. Stand the surround upright and check that the front face is flat and even at the joints.
  4. Move it around the stove, engage the panel hooks on the surround-bracket pins and push down to lock.
  5. Attach the fan controls to the inside of the right side panel with the two screws in the fan control mounting plate.
  6. Push the appliance back until the surround contacts the fireplace facing.
Don't let the wires contact the firebox or the mounting plate. They may melt.
Blower power
Plug the blower into a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug; never cut or remove the grounding prong. Wire to local codes (CSA C22.2 / ANSI/NFPA 70).
Install the firebricks
With the insert in its final position, fit the 20 full-size firebricks: rear wall under the rear brick rail first, then the floor, then the side walls under the brick retainers.

1. Place the first brick up under the rear brick rail and slide it to the far left or far right.
  2. Place 3 more bricks under the rear brick rail to complete the rear wall.
  3. Lay the floor bricks lengthwise, as shown in the manual's figure.
  4. On each side, set the first side-wall brick under the brick retainer, on top of the floor bricks, and slide it back against the rear bricks.
  5. Place three more bricks along that side wall the same way, then repeat on the opposite side.

Firebrick set 9"x4 1/2"x1 1/4" (20pcs.), part 80000620. Replace broken or missing bricks before use.

panels.title: Glass is dirty
items: Air control or damper turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low → check chimney height/diameter and for a plugged or restricted flue; provide outside air
Door gasket leakage → replace the gasket; if the latch is bent, consult dealer
Excessive creosote buildup → the same first three causes

panels.title: Low heat output
items: Fire too small → build a larger fire
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

panels.title: Won't burn overnight
items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter (see over-firing, p. 9)

panels.title: Stove won't burn
items: Combustion air blocked → check the outside air supply for obstruction; check the room air cover is removed
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean
Chimney oversized or otherwise unsuitable → consult dealer

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Before your very first fire, remove the retaining clip on the front of the baffle tubes and board.

  1. Move the air control lever all the way to the left (maximum firing rate) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox and criss-cross several pieces of dry kindling over it. Add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully in flames. Don't leave the fire unattended.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. When there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control for normal burning.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Build the fire right on the firebricks, with no grate or andirons, and keep the door closed while it burns.

Your first 2–3 fires

The paint bakes on during the first few fires and can give off smoke and fumes. Open windows and doors so the room is well ventilated, and follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with your insert. Smoke detectors may go off more often for a while. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
One lever sets the firing rate, meaning how hard the fire burns. Slide it left for more air (all the way left is the maximum firing rate) and right for less (all the way right is "Low").

  • After lighting or reloading, keep the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes, when most of the smoke is made. After about 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot without making excess smoke.
  • If smoke pours down across the glass (a "waterfall"), you turned the air down too soon or set it too low.
  • Every home is different. Find your best setting by trial and error, and note it for next time.
  • Use the all-the-way-left setting only for starting a fire or preheating a fresh load.
Don't over-fire. Pushing for more heat than the insert is designed for can permanently damage it and the chimney, and may void the warranty. An uncontrollable burn or a glowing red stove part or chimney means there's too much draft.

The lowest burn rate is set at the factory. Changing it is against federal regulations, and tampering with the air control voids the warranty.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
Adding wood

  1. Move the air control to high (lever left) and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. This prevents back puffing.
  3. Load dry logs of different shapes and sizes (18" is the ideal length), placed so air can flow between them, then close the door.

Smaller loads of two or three logs burn cleanest. Don't load wood so high that opening the door would be hazardous, and make sure no logs stick out where they could hit the glass.

Overnight burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the load completely on the maximum setting before you turn the air down for the night. Never try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting from coals

  1. Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Put a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door.
  2. Move the air control to high. The logs should start burning within a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air to your usual setting.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Your insert is designed to burn natural cordwood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or freshly cut wood.

  • Season wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources, and never within the insert's clearances.
  • Wet or green wood smoulders, makes heavy smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.
  • Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. It's dry if it burns on more than one side within one minute. It's damp if it turns black and lights within three minutes. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's soaked. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Wet or green wood, unseasoned wood, garbage, salt-water or treated wood, coal or charcoal, plywood, particleboard, cardboard or paper products, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, solvents, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products, construction or demolition debris, or anything containing rubber (including tires), plastic or asbestos. Burning these can release toxic fumes, or make the insert ineffective and cause excessive smoke. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Charcoal can give off carbon monoxide, an odourless gas that can kill. Never try to barbecue in the insert.

Note: The do-not-burn list (p. 7) names wet or green wood and unseasoned wood, and the chimney-fire advice (p. 6) says not to burn wet wood. The safety section (p. 4) says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to keep a good, strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and not to try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the insert is cold.

  • When the ash in the firebox gets 3" to 4" deep, wait until the fire has burned down and cooled, then take out the excess.
  • Leave about a 1" bed of ash on the firebox bottom. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Don't let ash build up over the combustion air openings at the front of the firebox (or at your fresh-air intake). It blocks the air flow.
Removing ashes often keeps embers from rolling out the door when you open it.

Disposing of ashes

Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container outside on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn. If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all cinders have thoroughly cooled. Don't put other waste in this container.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
If the glass darkens from slow burning or poor wood, clean it with fireplace glass cleaner once the insert is cold.

  • Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that might scratch.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood and a fairly clean chimney. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly, and it's building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Cracked or broken glass

Replace it before you use the insert again. Use only 5 mm ceramic glass, 9-1/4" x 13-1/4", from your dealer (replacement glass with clamps and gasket is part 80000616). Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out where they could hit the glass.

Hot glass will burn you. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote, a tar residue, in the chimney. When it ignites it burns extremely hot: over 2000°F inside the chimney.

  • Have the chimney and connector inspected at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Burn dry wood, load two or three logs at a time, and don't turn the air down too soon after loading.
  • Hotter fires leave less creosote. Mild weather and wet wood mean more frequent cleaning.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Close down the air control on the insert.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Get ready to evacuate. Everyone should know the plan and the meeting place outside.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks, and check combustibles around the chimney and roof.
Keep a fire extinguisher handy, and make sure everyone in your home knows these steps.

blower.title: Using the blower
blower.html:
Your insert comes with a variable-speed blower that circulates warm air into the room. Its control knob is on the lower right side edge of the surround panel.

  • On: turn the knob clockwise, then keep turning to find the speed you want.
  • Off: turn it counterclockwise past the click.
  • With the air control on "Low" (all the way right), run the blower on low. At any higher air setting, use whatever speed you like.

Keep it clean

Lift the surround to unhook it at the top and bottom of its sides, pull it toward you, then gently vacuum dust and hair from the blower inlets and motor. Clean it more often if your home is dusty or you have pets. You can do this yourself, but a qualified service technician can inspect the whole insert at the same time.

Note: p. 5 says to clean the blower a minimum of every six months; p. 20 says it requires annual cleaning.

The blower needs a properly grounded three-prong outlet. Never cut or remove the grounding prong, and unplug it before servicing.

care.title: Maintenance checklist
care.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and warping. Until you're experienced, also check the firebox daily for creosote buildup.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracks) · door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rails and their tabs · back of the airwash chamber · boost tube opening · top baffle boards · baffle tubes
ChimneyInspect at least every 2 months; clean as needed, at least 2 times a year
BlowerVacuum the inlets, grills and motor

When the chimney is cleaned, also check the top heat shield and its mounting bolt, the brick rails and the manifold. Replace baffle tubes that show cracks or breakage.

Note: p. 5 says to clean the blower a minimum of every six months; p. 20 says it requires annual cleaning.

Door gasket

The door seals with 5/8" medium-density fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure. Keep it in good condition and replace it when needed with the gasket kit from your True North dealer.

Running the insert with broken parts can damage other parts and voids your warranty. Use only parts supplied by the manufacturer.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
True North warrants the insert to the original consumer purchaser, for normal residential use. The warranty can't be transferred.

Firebox, castings, glass*3 years parts (1 year labour)
Electrical components and switches1 year parts and labour
Gaskets, paint (peeling), bricks, baffle tubes, baffle manifold, ceramic fibre board1 year (parts only)

*Glass is covered for thermal breakage only, not impact. A one-time replacement limit applies to all warranted parts.

Not covered

  • Damage from misuse, improper installation, lack of maintenance, over-firing, negligence, shipping accidents, power failures, downdrafts or venting problems.
  • Scratches, corrosion, warping or discoloration from over-firing, abrasives or chemical cleaners.
  • Defects caused by unauthorized parts, and service calls for an improper installation.

An authorized qualified technician must do the installation. To make a claim, contact your dealer with your dated bill of sale, the model name and the serial number (on the certification label or the manual cover). You can register at truenorthstoves.com/register.

specOutput.title: Heat output
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output13,900 to 29,200 btu/hr
Peak BTU/hr output55,000

EPA range: CSA B415 efficiency with the burn rates from the low and high EPA tests on Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. Peak: the maximum one-hour high burn rate from the high-burn EPA test at the BTU content of cord wood (8600 btu/lb).

The introduction (p. 2) gives the tested range unrounded: 13,931 to 29,208 Btu/hr.

specEmis.title: Emissions & efficiency
specEmis.html:
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
HHV tested efficiency72.7%
LHV tested efficiency78%
Maker's website: Efficiency 73% (HHV).

Weighted averages tested to CSA B415; HHV includes the energy needed to vaporize the water in the fuel. Meets the EPA 2020 crib wood particulate standard (label: test Method 28R, 1.6 g/hr). The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered (p. 9).

specWood.title: Fuel & wood length
specWood.html:
Maximum wood length20 inches
Ideal wood length18 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Maker's website: Log Size (max.) 18 in. The website lists the manual's ideal length as its maximum; the manual's maximum is 20 inches.

The specifications (p. 3) give a maximum wood length of 20 inches and an ideal length of 18 inches. The operating instructions (p. 8) say to use wood of different shapes, diameters and lengths up to 18" (457mm), the ideal length.

Cordwood only. Burn directly on the firebricks; no grates or andirons.

specFlue.title: Flue liner & chimney
specFlue.html:
LinerListed 6" stainless steel, rigid or flex
CanadaFull liner required: CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640, class 3
USALiner to UL-1777, or direct flue connection
Min. chimney height15' recommended (p. 14)

The full liner runs from the flue collar to the top of the chimney; Pacific Energy highly recommends it for the safest installation and correct draft. Connect only to a code-approved masonry chimney with a listed flue liner, never to a flue serving another appliance or to an air distribution duct. Below the recommended chimney height, starting or operating problems may occur.

To clean and inspect the chimney, disconnect the liner from the insert; remove the baffle boards only if that isn't possible, and never operate without them (p. 19).

specFireplace.title: Minimum fireplace size
specFireplace.html:
Width at the front29"
Width at the back22"
Height20 1/4"
Depth18"

The installation section (p. 13) calls for an approved masonry wood fireplace built to NFPA 211 (CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada). Repair cracks or loose mortar first, lock the damper open or remove it, and have the chimney cleaned. Don't remove bricks or mortar, except masonry or steel (including the damper plate) from the smoke shelf and damper frame where needed for a liner, without weakening the structure.

Note: p. 13 and the label (p. 25) say the insert shall not be installed in a factory-built fireplace; the clearance section on p. 11 gives clearances "when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace."

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Adjacent sidewall*12 in. (label: 16 1/2 in.)
Side facing*, max 2 in. deep8 1/2 in. (label: 13 in.)
Mantel / top facing, max 12 in. deep15 in.
Ceiling, from base of unit54 in.

*Measured from the side of the stove. Mantel and top facing are measured from the firebox top.

Note: p. 11 gives side clearances of 12 in. to an adjacent sidewall and 8 1/2 in. to side facing; the rating label on p. 25 gives 16 1/2 IN and 13 IN, also "measured from side of unit". The 15 in. mantel / top facing clearance agrees.

The insert's overall dimensions are shown only as a drawing on this page; take them from the manual.

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
USA (NFPA 211)

Hearth raised 1" above combustible floor16" in front, 8" beyond each side
Hearth flush with combustible floor21" in front, 8" beyond each side
Ember protection16" to the front, 8" to the sides of the unit

Canada (CAN/CSA-B365)

Hearth (may be flush)16" in front, 8" beyond each side
Ember protection18" to the front, 8" to the sides of the unit

Hearth extensions are measured from the fireplace opening; ember protection is non-combustible material over the combustible floor in front of the insert. The label (p. 25) also calls for Type 1 floor protection approved to UL1618, minimum 20GA steel, adjacent to the hearth.

specElec.title: Blower electrical
specElec.html:
Installation section (p. 21)115V, 0.5A 60 Hz
Rating label, English (p. 25)115V, 60HZ, 0.6 AMP
Rating label, French (p. 25)115V, 60HZ, 1,1 AMP
Note: p. 21 gives the blower current as 0.5A; the rating label on p. 25 gives 0.6 AMP in its English text and 1,1 AMP in its French text.

Use a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug; don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Wire to local codes, or CSA C22.2 (Canada) / ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). Route the power cord away from the unit and keep the wires off the firebox and mounting plate.

conflicts.issue: Maximum log length: specifications give Maximum Wood Length 20 inches / Ideal 18 inches (p. 3); Normal Operation says wood 'up to 18" (457mm)' (p. 8).
conflicts.reason: Both fit: p. 3 lists a maximum (20 inches) and an ideal (18 inches) wood length, and the p. 8 loading instruction 'up to 18" (457mm)' matches the ideal length. Shown as 18 in. ideal / 20 in. maximum per the True North log-length rule (Ben, Oct 9).

conflicts.issue: Side clearances: adjacent sidewall 12 in. and side facing 8 1/2 in. (p. 11 text and Figure 3) vs 16 1/2 IN and 13 IN on the rating label (p. 25), both 'measured from side of stove/unit'. Mantel/top facing 15 in. agrees.
Blower electrical rating: 115V, 0.5A 60 Hz (p. 21) vs 115V, 60HZ, 0.6 AMP on the label's English text and 1,1 AMP on its French text (p. 25).
Fireplace type: 'shall not be installed in a factory-built fireplace' (p. 13; label p. 25) vs clearances given 'when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace' (p. 11). Also shown in step0.
Blower cleaning interval: 'a minimum every six months' (p. 5) vs 'requires annual cleaning' (p. 20). Also shown in the care drawer.

Wet or unseasoned wood: the do-not-burn list on p. 7 names 'Wet or green wood' and 'Unseasoned wood' and p. 6 says 'Do not burn wet wood', but p. 4 (item 1) says 'If you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures. Do not attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood.' The guide shows both in an amber note in the wood drawer.

review.notes: Single doc: Installation & Operation Manual 100000127 (230726-28), 28 physical pages; p. 27 is blank and p. 28 is the back cover. Wood insert, so no ignition system, gas-smell block, French-only safety text or offset-font text; nothing was translated or decoded. Stove Dimensions (p. 11) and the clearance/hearth figures (pp. 11, 12, 14) are drawings with unlabeled numbers; overall dimensions were not transcribed (specClear says they are a drawing on p. 11). p. 2 gives the EPA range unrounded (13,931 to 29,208 Btu/hr) and p. 3 rounded (13,900 to 29,200); shown as a note, not a conflict. Metric oddities, inches agree: US ember protection printed 16"(457mm) on p. 12 (label: 405 MM / 16 IN); Canada ember protection 18"(450mm) on p. 12 vs 460 MM / 18 IN on the label. Guide uses inches only. Figure 5 caption on p. 12 reads 'US 2in Drop hearth' while the text, the figure's own 'Min. 1" drop', p. 14 and the label all say 1"; guide follows the text. The label heading for the side clearances pairs 'measured from side of unit' with French 'mesures de l'ouverture de porte', which names a different reference point; worth checking when resolving the side-clearance conflict. Catalog values the manual does not state (unverified): firebox_cu_ft 2.0, burn_time_hr_max 8, combustion_type non-catalytic, surround 38 x 27 in, backing plate 48 x 32 in, extension 46 x 31 in (manual lists Surround Extension Set 31250001 and Oversized Trimable Backing Plate Set 31120002 without sizes). No weight, firebox volume or burn time in the manual. No error/code table, so codes is empty.
